claims.analysis_en: According to the release, the remains were first discovered in June 2010 at Hill 490 on Maebongsan Mountain in Junggu-ri, Hyoryeong-myeon, Gunwi-gun. A specialist MAKRI team subsequently recovered the left and right femurs. The release does not describe other skeletal elements. Discovery in 2010 should not be confused with the much later identification of Private Jo Cha-sang.
source_quotes_ko: ◦국방부 유해발굴감식단(이하 국유단, 단장 전병희)은 2010년 6월 대구광역시 군위군 효령면 중구리 매봉산 일대에서 발굴한 유해의 신원을 국군 제6사단 소속의 고 조차상 일병으로 확인했다.
□ 고인의 유해는 2010년 6월 군위군 중구리 매봉산 490고지에서 유해발굴을 진행하던 중 최초 식별됐으며, 이후 국유단 전문 발굴팀이 고인의 좌우 넓적다리뼈를 수습했다.

claims.analysis_en: The release states that a DNA sample was collected from the family in 2012, but that the analytical techniques then available did not confirm a family relationship. It reports that additional testing of residual samples in March 2026 confirmed that the deceased and Jo Ok-ran were siblings. The document cites technical limitations for the initial failure; it does not establish whether any other factors contributed. These conclusions remain attributed to the issuing authority.
claims.heading_en: DNA Identification: Prior Failure and Subsequent Confirmation
source_quotes_ko: □ 유가족 유전자 시료는 2012년 채취했으나, 당시 유전자 분석 기술로는 가족관계를 확인할 수 없었다.
◦국유단은 고인의 유해에서 추출한 유전자와 유가족 유전자 시료를 분석했으나, 안타깝게도 당시 유전자 분석 기술로는 가족관계를 확인할 수 없었다. 올해 3월, 유해시료 및 유가족 유전자 잔여 시료를 추가 검사한 결과 고 조차상 일병과 조옥란 씨가 남매관계임을 확인할 수 있었다.

claims.analysis_en: The release states that Private Jo Cha-sang was born in August 1930 in Bubuk-myeon, Miryang City, enlisted at the Army Training Center on July 17, 1950, and was killed in action on August 14, 1950, in the 'Battle near Gunwi-Uiheung.' The release further describes that battle as a defensive engagement by the 7th Regiment, ROK 6th Division, against North Korean 1st and 8th Division forces from August 13 to 28, 1950. These biographical and operational details are presented as established facts by the issuing authority; they are government assertions and are not independently verified by these sources.
claims.heading_en: Reported Service Record and Circumstances of Death
source_quotes_ko: ◦고인은 1930년 8월 경상남도 밀양시 부북면에서 9남매(7남 2녀) 중 장남으로 태어났다. 이후 1950년 7월 17일 육군훈련소로 입대한 고인은 제6사단 소속으로 적과 싸우다 1950년 8월 14일 ‘군위-의흥 부근 전투’에서 전사했다.
◦‘군위-의흥 부근 전투’는 국군 6사단 7연대가 1950년 8월 13일부터 28일까지 대구 군위군 효령면 미사리 일대에서 북한군 1·8사단의 공격을 방어한 전투다.

claims.analysis_en: The release characterises Private Jo Cha-sang as the fourteenth individual whose identity MAKRI confirmed in the year of the release, and the 282nd fallen ROK soldier returned to family since the programme commenced in April 2000. These figures are presented as programme metrics by the issuing authority and reflect the government's own accounting; they cannot be verified from the source material alone.
source_quotes_ko: ◦고인은 올해 국유단이 열네 번째로 신원을 확인한 호국영웅이며, 2000년 4월 유해발굴사업 개시 이래 가족의 품으로 돌아간 282번째 국군 전사자다.

claims.analysis_en: The release states that the return ceremony was held at the home of Jo Ok-ran in Gimhae City in accordance with the bereaved family's wishes, and that MAKRI Director Jeon Byeong-hui presented the family with a National Defense Hero Return plaque, an identity confirmation notice, and a box containing excavated personal effects. The release also records a statement attributed to Jo Ok-ran referencing her mother's dying wish that her brother's remains be found and interred at a national cemetery. These are attributed statements and reported procedural facts; the emotional characterisation reflects the family representative's quoted words as rendered in the release.
claims.heading_en: Return Ceremony Conduct and Items Presented
source_quotes_ko: □ 이번 귀환 행사는 유가족 뜻에 따라 경상남도 김해시에 위치한 고인의 여동생인 조옥란 씨의 자택에서 진행됐다.
◦유가족 대표 조옥란(1946년생, 80세) 씨는 “오빠 유해를 찾았다고 하니 심장이 덜덜 떨려서 잠을 못 잤다”며 “엄마가 돌아가실 때 나한테 ‘너라도 꼭 오빠 유해를 찾아서 국립묘지에 안장하라’고 유언을 남기셨는데 이렇게 찾게 해주셔서 감사하다”고 소회를 밝혔다.
◦행사를 주관한 전병희 국유단장은 유가족에게 호국영웅 귀환 패와 신원확인 통지서, 발굴 유품이 담긴 호국의 얼 함(函)을 전달했다. 이어 고인의 참전 경로와 유해발굴 경과, 신원확인까지의 과정을 설명했다.

claims.analysis_en: The release includes a public appeal stating that DNA sample collection is open to relatives up to the eighth degree of kinship on both paternal and maternal sides, and that a reward of 10 million won is payable upon confirmed identification. It also notes that individuals with limited mobility may contact the number 1577-5625 for in-person sample collection. The release further asserts that finding bereaved families is becoming increasingly difficult due to the aging of veterans and their relatives. These are policy statements and programme descriptions issued by the government authority; their operational accuracy is not assessable from the source text alone.
claims.heading_en: Public Participation Appeal and Programme Access Information
source_quotes_ko: ◦유가족 유전자 시료 채취는 6·25 전사자의 유가족으로서 전사자 기준으로 친·외가 8촌까지 신청 가능합니다. 제공하신 유전자 정보를 통해 전사자의 신원이 확인될 경우 1,000만 원의 포상금을 지급합니다. 자세한 내용은 “정부 24” 홈페이지에서도 확인하실 수 있습니다.
◦6·25전쟁이 발발한 지 오랜 시간이 흐른 현재 참전용사와 유가족의 고령화 등으로 유가족 찾기는 점점 더 어려워지고 있습니다. 하루하루 시간과의 싸움을 벌이고 있는 만큼 국민 여러분의 적극적인 관심과 참여가 절실합니다.
◦국유단은 전국 각지에 계신 유가족분들을 찾기 위해 오늘도 최선의 노력을 다하고 있습니다. 유전자 시료를 제공하고 싶어도 거동이 불편해 참여가 어려운 분들께서는 대표번호 1577-5625(오! 6·25)로 언제든 연락 주시면 직접 찾아뵙고 유전자 시료를 채취해 드리고 있습니다.  <끝>

analysis.heading_en: MAKRI Press Release: Identification and Return Ceremony of the Late Private Jo Cha-sang, ROK 6th Division (October 15, 2026)
analysis.limitations_en: All factual claims in this analysis derive exclusively from a single government press release issued by MAKRI. Biographical details, service records, battle descriptions, DNA analysis conclusions, programme statistics, and quoted statements are reproduced as attributed government assertions and have not been cross-checked against independent sources. Machine translations are unreviewed and may contain rendering errors. The release date of October 15, 2026, is noted as stated in the source; no independent verification of this date or any other claim is possible from the provided material. No inference is drawn regarding intent, downstream effects, or any approval processes not described in the source. The captured Korean source header gives October 15, 2026 as a Wednesday, although that date was a Thursday; the body of the release correctly states Thursday. Both header translations preserve and identify the discrepancy.
analysis.thesis_en: The Ministry of National Defense Agency for KIA Recovery and Identification (MAKRI) announced the identification of remains excavated in 2010 as those of Private Jo Cha-sang, and held a return ceremony on October 15, 2026, in Gimhae City. The identification was achieved through re-analysis of previously inconclusive DNA samples, approximately 76 years after the soldier's reported death in August 1950.

translations.text_en: Press Release
Release Time
15 October 2026, 11:00 (the Korean source header prints Wednesday; 15 October 2026 was Thursday)
Distribution
15 October 2026, 08:30 (the Korean source header prints Wednesday; 15 October 2026 was Thursday)
"I will fulfill my mother's dying wish to find my eldest brother's remains — 76 years later"
- Remains recovered in Gunwi, Daegu in 2010 identified as Private Jo Cha-sang, attached to the 6th Division
- Killed in action in August 1950 in the 'Battle near Gunwi-Uiheung'… returned to the arms of younger sister Jo Ok-ran

□ On October 15 (Thursday), a 'Return of a National Defense Hero' ceremony was held in Gimhae City, Gyeongsangnam-do, for the late Private Jo Cha-sang, who is stated to have given his life at the age of 20 during the Korean War.

◦ The Ministry of National Defense Agency for KIA Recovery and Identification (hereinafter MAKRI, Director Jeon Byeong-hui) confirmed that remains excavated in June 2010 from the area of Maebongsan Mountain, Junggu-ri, Hyoryeong-myeon, Gunwi-gun, Daegu Metropolitan City, belong to the late Private Jo Cha-sang of the Republic of Korea Army 6th Division.

◦ The deceased is stated to be the fourteenth national defense hero whose identity MAKRI confirmed this year, and the 282nd fallen ROK soldier to be returned to the arms of family since the commencement of the remains excavation project in April 2000.

□ The remains were first discovered in June 2010 during an excavation at Hill 490 on Maebongsan Mountain in Junggu-ri, Gunwi-gun; MAKRI’s specialist excavation team subsequently recovered the deceased’s left and right femurs. Identification of the soldier came later.
□ A DNA sample was collected from the bereaved family in 2012; however, the DNA analysis technology available at the time was unable to confirm the family relationship.

◦ In June 2012, younger sister Jo Ok-ran (born 1946, then 66 years old), upon learning of the Korean War fallen soldiers' remains excavation project, visited the Gimhae City Public Health Center to participate in DNA sample collection in order to find her eldest brother.

◦ MAKRI analyzed the DNA extracted from the remains of the deceased together with the DNA sample from the bereaved family; however, regrettably, the DNA analysis technology available at the time was unable to confirm the family relationship. In March of this year, additional testing of the remaining remains sample and the bereaved family's residual DNA sample confirmed that the late Private Jo Cha-sang and Jo Ok-ran are siblings.

□ The deceased, a native of Miryang, Gyeongsangnam-do, is stated to have participated in the war as a member of the ROK Army 6th Division and to have been killed in action in August 1950 in the 'Battle near Gunwi-Uiheung.'

◦ The deceased was born in August 1930 in Bubuk-myeon, Miryang City, Gyeongsangnam-do, as the eldest of nine siblings (7 sons and 2 daughters). He subsequently enlisted at the Army Training Center on July 17, 1950, and is stated to have fought against the enemy as a member of the 6th Division before being killed in action on August 14, 1950, in the 'Battle near Gunwi-Uiheung.'

◦ The 'Battle near Gunwi-Uiheung' is described as a battle in which the 7th Regiment of the ROK Army 6th Division defended against attacks by the North Korean Army's 1st and 8th Divisions in the area of Misari, Hyoryeong-myeon, Gunwi-gun, Daegu, from August 13 to 28, 1950.
□ The return ceremony was held, in accordance with the wishes of the bereaved family, at the home of the deceased's younger sister, Jo Ok-ran, located in Gimhae City, Gyeongsangnam-do.

◦ Bereaved family representative Jo Ok-ran (born 1946, age 80) stated, "When I heard that my brother's remains had been found, my heart trembled so much I could not sleep," and added, "When our mother was dying, she left me a dying wish saying, 'You must be the one to find your brother's remains and have him interred at the national cemetery.' I am grateful that we have been able to find him like this."

◦ MAKRI Director Jeon Byeong-hui, who presided over the ceremony, presented the bereaved family with the National Defense Hero Return plaque, the identity confirmation notice, and the Hoguk-ui Eol Ham (a box containing excavated personal effects). He then explained the deceased's route of participation in the war, the progress of the remains excavation, and the process leading to identity confirmation.

◦ Director Jeon Byeong-hui stated, "I express deep respect for the noble sacrifice and dedication of the deceased, who gave his life for his country at a young age," and emphasized, "We will continue to do our utmost to recover the remains of national defense heroes to the very end, and to heal the pain of the remaining bereaved families by concentrating our efforts on collecting DNA samples from family members and other such measures."

□ The active interest and participation of the public is urgently needed for the identification of Korean War fallen soldiers who gave their lives for the Republic of Korea but have not yet been returned to the arms of their families.

◦ DNA sample collection for bereaved families is open to relatives of Korean War fallen soldiers up to the eighth degree of kinship on both the paternal and maternal sides, based on the fallen soldier. If the identity of a fallen soldier is confirmed through the provided DNA information, a reward of 10 million won will be paid. Further details can also be found on the 'Government 24' website.

◦ As a great deal of time has passed since the outbreak of the Korean War, finding bereaved families is becoming increasingly difficult due to factors such as the aging of war veterans and their families. As every day is a race against time, the active interest and participation of the public is urgently needed.

◦ MAKRI is doing its utmost today as well to find bereaved families located throughout the country. Those who wish to provide a DNA sample but find it difficult to participate due to limited mobility are welcome to contact the main number 1577-5625 (Oh! 6·25) at any time, and staff will visit in person to collect the DNA sample. <End>
